plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DESeq2 DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12000-gene x 6-sample raw integer count matrix from STAR/featureCounts (human liver, 3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch), with metadata.csv holding the condition label. The library strandedness was never recorded, and only the final count table was delivered — no BAM/alignment files or featureCounts summary are present in the inputs, so a genuine strand inference (e.g. RSeQC infer_experiment, which needs aligned reads against an annotation) cannot be executed here. This gap cannot be closed retrospectively from a count matrix alone, so the plan treats it as a persistent caveat rather than a blocker: it substitutes the best available proxy checks (library-size/detected-gene consistency across the 6 samples, and a liver-tissue marker sanity check) to catch a catastrophic assignment failure, while stating explicitly that a partial antisense/strand mis-assignment for individual overlapping gene pairs cannot be ruled out or corrected. Because a wrong strand setting, if applied uniformly across all 6 samples (single batch, same protocol), acts as a shared technical factor and does not by itself manufacture a treated-vs-control difference except for genes with an antisense-overlapping neighbor whose own expression differs by treatment — this caveat is carried into the final report rather than dropped. Downstream: minimal low-count pre-filtering, median-of-ratios normalization inside DESeq2 (with a stated GC-content/gene-length bias diagnostic, since the bias-correction tools cqn/EDASeq are not available in this environment), an explicit reference level (control) and named contrast (treated vs control), a DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05. With 3 vs 3 replicates the design has low power for anything but large effects, so the plan states this explicitly rather than loosening the threshold, and adds an edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check (the recommended second method at this replicate count) to report the overlap of the two gene sets as the higher-confidence subset. The Wald statistic ranks the full gene list for a preranked fgsea against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection first, then WikiPathways human and Reactome human as separate follow-up passes (each release stated, not merged), since the significant-gene list at n=3/group is expected to be too short for a sound over-representation test. A final report consolidates the gene tables (shrunken and unshrunken log2FC), fit diagnostics, the two-method overlap, the enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, the power caveat, and the strandedness/count-fidelity caveat, plus a full reproducibility record.

steps.question: What is the complete, reproducible answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control liver samples', with all quality, power, and strandedness caveats stated alongside the results?
steps.context: Consolidates the QC/sanity checks (T1S1), the bias diagnostic (T1S2), the DESeq2 and edgeR gene tables and their overlap (T1S3, T1S4), and the three-collection fgsea enrichment (T2S1) into one report.
acceptance_criteria: States up front, before any gene table, that the library strandedness was unrecorded and could not be inferred (no BAM/alignment files available), and summarizes what the T1S1 proxy checks did and did not rule out
States the expected power of the DESeq2/edgeR tests at n=3/group before the gene tables

Reports method, package versions (DESeq2, apeglm, edgeR, fgsea), the design formula, the named contrast (treated vs control, control reference), the adjusted-p-value and BH thresholds used, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes per method
Presents the DESeq2 gene table with unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, and padj, ranked by shrunken log2FoldChange
Presents the MA plot and dispersion plot from T1S3 with a one-line statement of what each shows
Reports the DESeq2-vs-edgeR intersection as the high-confidence gene set and the per-method-only genes as secondary, per T1S4
Reports the fgsea results per collection (Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways) with database version, rank metric, universe, and size window stated, plus leading-edge genes per significant set

Includes a full reproducibility record: session info, package versions, random seeds used, and the version/release of every reference collection consulted (Hallmark 2026.1, Reactome release as staged, WikiPathways 2026.07.10, and any tissue-expression reference used in T1S1/T1S2)
constraints: Do not omit the strandedness/count-fidelity caveat from the top of the report
Do not present the enrichment result as validated biology; label it a hypothesis per the enrichment method-dependence caveat
caveats: This report cannot certify that the counts are strand-correct; it can only report what the available proxy checks did and did not find

grounding.reason: Report-stage rules require the power statement (R-0094), the two-method overlap (R-0042), shrunken+unshrunken LFC (R-0085), the two fit diagnostics (R-0087), full method/version/threshold reporting (R-0041), enrichment database/version/metric/universe/window reporting (R-0051), the method-dependence caveat (R-0055), leading-edge genes (R-0105), and the full reproducibility record (R-0086).
